title: Needle out
note: Fictional patient. Doses and energies are quoted from the 2025 AHA guidelines (and the ERC where named) for recognition; your unit protocol, crash-cart stock and the attending nephrologist come first. Simulation success is an educational result, not a prediction of patient survival.
intro: Bacolod City, 4:15 p.m. Mrs. Gloria Santiago, 74, asleep under a thick blanket in her third hour. Blood is dripping from under the blanket onto a wet floor. The machine shows no alarm. She is pale and hard to wake.

n1.prompt: What do you do in the first ten seconds?

choices.text: Stop the pump, clamp both sides, press firmly on the site, shout for help.
choices.feedback: A quiet machine proves nothing; stop the loss first. Lift the blanket: the venous needle is out. Press with gloved hands and gauze.

choices.text: Reinsert the needle and continue, so the session can finish and she keeps her dry weight target.
choices.then: The charge nurse stops you; pump off, clamp, pressure.

choices.text: Check the machine first; it shows no alarm, so the bleeding must be minor.
choices.feedback: The venous pressure alarm can stay silent when a needle is out.
choices.then: You lift the blanket and see the needle out.

n2.scene: Pressure 76/42, heart rate 128. Large pool of blood.

choices.text: Flat, oxygen, call the physicians, new IV for saline, estimate the loss.
choices.feedback: Hemorrhagic shock: volume, help, and a safe floor. Not the open line; assign a watcher and dry the floor.

choices.text: Return the circuit blood through the open line end to replace what she has lost.
choices.feedback: Blood is never returned through an open line end.

choices.text: Cardiac arrest from hemorrhage: compressions, pads, fluids, early transfer for blood.
choices.feedback: The cause guides treatment during CPR. The arrest algorithm as usual; dry the floor before kneeling or shocking.

choices.text: Keep pressing the site and wait for the physician, since stopping the bleeding comes first.

end.title: 4:45 p.m.
end.text: With fluids and CPR she regains a pulse and is transferred for blood. The unit changes its blanket rule: access arms stay visible.

debrief:
What this case teaches

  • Lift the blanket; machines can miss dislodgement.
  • Stop, clamp, press; never reinsert or return through an open end.
  • Arrest from hemorrhage: CPR plus volume and early blood.
